title: Only write horoscopes for dates with matched events

history.detail:
PASS: Gate-1 audit of d898448 (HEAD). Sprint file re-read fresh; unchanged since b60527f (planning) apart from 3f2b318's lifecycle status line and folder move. The prerequisite fast-lane fix (71b8e88, halos and long event words) landed first, as the Dependencies section requires.

HANDOFF (new CLAUDE.md standard, 4ad01db): read with git show d898448:docs/handoffs/sprint-39.md. It is present at the audited commit, has a "## Round 1" section, and quotes "VERIFY PASS (lint, typecheck, test, build) exit=0 (34 test files, 423 tests)". QA1's own run at d898448 matches exactly: exit=0, 34 files, 423 tests. R12's screenshots are committed under docs/handoffs/sprint-39/: 12 PNGs, covering before and after for an unmatched date at desktop and at 390, JS off, a followed link, saved-unmatched, and /reading/[id] including null events. This is the first sprint where QA1 could check the handoff itself.

THE RULE: lib/events/matched.ts. hasMatchedEvents is true only for matchedYear === true, the same strictness as Sprint 30's SQL predicate; the string "true", null and a missing key are all rejected, and tested. unwritableReason gives null for writable, the R5 lead for null events, and the R3/R4 lead for unmatched. Every check reads this one rule: cast, generate, lookupSavedHoroscope, eventsLabel, eventsStatusLabel, EventYear, and horoscopeAvailability.

R1 MET: EventYear in ReadingView links only when the payload is not matched AND linkableEventDate returns a date, using next/link with href=datePagePath(target). linkableEventDate rejects non-integer, negative and over-9999 years, pads to 4 digits, keeps isoDate's "-MM-DD", and lets parseDatePageParam decide range and leap days. eventDate is the page date, or the row's event_date on /reading/[id]. A grep of the code diff for a hand-built "/date/" path finds nothing (exit 1). Matched dates keep plain spans, and this is tested.
R2 MET: an unmatched payload gives "No recorded events for this day." The null and matched texts are byte-identical to before (checked in the diff). The rendered events label is only used for an empty list.
R3, R4, R5 MET: unavailableMessage returns the leads and next sentences verbatim from the sprint file. Selection: lookupFailed for null; unmatched with hasLinkableYear (R3) only when at least one event year is linkable; otherwise R4, covering zero events, every event before 1700, and 29 February with no leap year in range. Each case is a named test against the exact text.
R6 MET: on both pages, availability is checked first in the JSX ternary, ahead of the outage notice, the cast form, the disabled panel and the saved horoscope. It is decided from events alone, with no database call. HoroscopeUnavailableSection is a server component with no form, keeping the "The reading" heading and a status label. Tests cover HOROSCOPE_ENABLED off and a failed saved-lookup still showing the message, and check that no write form is present (only the picker's GET form remains).
R7 MET, but see Q1 below. lookupSavedHoroscope reports a found row with unmatched or null events as "none", so loadDatePage falls through to a fresh fetchEvents, and availability then applies to that fetch. Every place a horoscope renders was enumerated by grep:
- app/date/[date]/page.tsx line 98 (reached only when availability is writable, and the saved row is matched by construction);
- app/reading/[id]/page.tsx line 105 (behind its own availability check);
- ReadingView.tsx line 523, the DisabledReadingSection path, reached only after the availability branch on both pages.
app/api contains only health, with no horoscope. There is no migration (supabase/ is unchanged at d898448), and the render path still only calls lookupSavedHoroscope's RPC and fetchEvents, so it writes nothing.
R8 MET: in castHoroscopeForDate, unwritableReason(events) runs immediately after the server's own fetchEvents(isoDate) and before insertReading. It never reads the form. The order is: disabled, then existing lookup, then positions, then fetch, then REFUSE, then insert, then generate. The test asserts failure, fetchEvents called with the date, and writer.from, insert and rpc plus generate all not called, for both unmatched and null. It also asserts that a saved horoscope on an unmatched row does not short-circuit the cast to ok:true.
R9 MET: generateAndPersistHoroscope refuses right after the disabled check, before buildReadingModel and generateHoroscope. /reading/[id]'s action reaches OpenAI only through it. The test spies on generateHoroscope and asserts it is never called, with no rpc, for unmatched, the string "true", and null.
R10 MET: /reading/[id] computes availability from the row's stored events and event_date, ahead of the generate form and the disabled panel. Tests cover unmatched with linkable years (linked by the row's month and day), every event before 1700, null, and disabled.
R11 MET: every listed case exists as a named test: years 1699 and 2101, the ends 1700 and 2100, 29 February in 1900, 1901, 1904 and 2000, years 999, 44 and 5 (padded), BC and fractional years, each message case, and both refusals. The handoff also reports a mutation check: removing each guard in turn fails its own tests.
R12 MET: see HANDOFF above.

Code quality: small, pure decision functions; one rule module; and no duplicated path, glyph or message text. The status-label override on ReadingHeader is minimal. CSS: a padded and negative-margin tap target, 45px on phones. Errors: refusals return through the existing failure path with nothing swallowed.

ANSWERS TO DEV TEAM'S QUESTIONS:
Q1, the app-side R7 guard. It is acceptable against the SPRINT FILE: R7 says a matched reading "may still be shown" and leaves the route to Dev Team. But it does NOT fully match the user's recorded decision. docs/decisions.md, 23 Nov, item 2, says '"Newest with a horoscope wins" now applies among matched rows only.' Read literally, that requires showing the older matched horoscope in the mixed case.
- What actually happens: get_reading_by_date returns only the newest row with a horoscope. If that row is unmatched, the app reports none, and an older matched horoscope is unreachable. If the fresh lookup is matched, the page then offers to write a duplicate.
- I am not failing it. The sprint file is the audit spec and permits it, the handoff disclosed it plainly, and it needs pre-existing mixed data that the old one-per-date cast guard made rare.
- ROUTED TO MASTER CONTROLLER: the sprint file and decisions.md disagree. If the user holds the decision literally, that is a follow-up sprint, needing a migration to displayed_readings() and updated Sprint 28/30 database tests. Not this one.
Q2, straight quotes. Matching the sprint file's quoted text was correct: the acceptance criterion says "matches the quoted wording exactly". If the user wants curly typography to match the rest of the page, Master Controller amends the wording; it is not a code defect.

HUMAN PREREQUISITE (already in the sprint file, restated so it isn't missed): the user runs the SQL query in the sprint file's Human Prerequisites and gives LiveQA one or two unmatched dates with a saved horoscope, and a reading id, for steps 5 and 6. LiveQA has no database access.

No known-failing tests.
commit=d898448 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for d8984489199f0d12482b6b6c4b6d8603e62ca315 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: PASS (round 1). Every LiveQA step was run.
- Production: steps 1, 2, 5, 6 and 7.
- A local production build of the shipped commit: steps 4 and 8.
- Step 3 has no real production date. The rendering was shown locally, and the sprint file lets the unit
  tests carry that case.
No defects. Two observations are for Master Controller (below).

Tested 2026-11-23, about 22:20 to 23:00 UTC.
Shipped commit d898448. Production serves the pushed tip 8fa4781: /api/health/db reports status ok,
connected true, and commit 8fa4781, with migrationVersion unchanged at
20261122152710_navigation_exact_date_readings. git diff --stat d898448 8fa4781 touches only
docs/sprints/state/sprint-39.json.
CI: runs 45277004539 (d898448) and 45277982608 (8fa4781). Both succeeded.

Tools:
- Headless Chromium (Playwright 1.57) at 1280x900 and at 390x844 (isMobile, hasTouch), with JS on and off.
- curl against the served HTML.
- A fresh git clone at d898448 in a scratch directory, not my working tree: npm ci exit=0 and npm run
  build exit=0, then next start.

STEP 1, unmatched date with linkable events: PASS.
On /date/2031-05-09:
- The status reads "on this day, other years".
- All 5 years are links, each with an aria-label:
  - 2023 to /date/2023-05-09, "Go to 9 May 2023";
  - 2012, 2005, 2001 and 1992, each to its own -05-09 date.
- The reading section reads, verbatim: "The reading NO EXACT-DATE EVENTS We have no recorded events for
  this exact date, so we can't write an accurate horoscope for it. Pick a different date above, or choose
  one of the years listed under "What happened" to go to that date instead."
- The only form is the GET /date picker. There is no POST form, no reveal details and no write button.
- The same holds with JS off.
Mixed links, seen on the local build against my stand-in database: a stored row with years 2023, 1992,
1605 and 1415 renders 2023 and 1992 as links and 1605 and 1415 as plain text.
Matched control: /date/2023-05-09 has one year, "2023", as plain text with no anchor.
Screenshots: s39-2031-05-09-events-390.png and s39-2031-05-09-view-390.png.

STEP 2, follow a year link: PASS.
- A real click (desktop) and a real tap (390) on "2023" arrived at /date/2023-05-09.
- The status there reads "this exact date".
- The write option is present: a "Reveal the horoscope" button inside a POST multipart form, seen in the
  served HTML.
- Nothing was written; I did not submit it on production.
- Link boxes are 62x31 on desktop and 52x45 on the phone, underlined in the green link colour.

STEP 3, nothing to link to (Requirement 4): no real production date found. Rendering shown locally.
Production dates tried, each showing all-linkable years and Requirement 3:
- 2028-02-29, 2032-02-29 and 2096-02-29: years 2012, 2008, 2004, 2004, 1996, all leap years, so all
  linkable;
- 2099-02-28, 2100-12-31 and 1700-01-01.
A scan of Wikipedia's onthisday/selected feed for all 366 days was rate-limited (HTTP 429), and I stopped
it on the user's instruction:
- 21 days were read;
- the fewest events on any of them was 13;
- none had an unlinkable year in its first five.
The feed lists newest first, so real data is unlikely to produce this case.
On the local build, with a stand-in feed (see step 4):
- 01/01 returning only years 1605 and 1415: /date/2031-01-01 shows them as plain text, with the message
  "...accurate horoscope for it. Pick a different date above." and no second sentence.
- 01/02 returning an empty list: /date/2031-01-02 shows the events label "No recorded events for this
  day." and the same message.

STEP 4, failed lookup: PASS, on the local production build of d898448.
- api.wikimedia.org and wikipedia.org were blocked at the resolver: a dns.lookup preload throws ENOTFOUND,
  and the server log shows "getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.wikimedia.org".
- The Supabase URL pointed at an unreachable port, so the database failed too.
- /date/2023-05-09, 2031-05-09 and 1969-07-20 all show "The reading EVENTS UNAVAILABLE The events for this
  date couldn't be loaded, so the horoscope can't be written right now. Try again in a few minutes."
- The events label reads "No events looked up for this reading." There is no POST form.
R6 precedence, on the local build with HOROSCOPE_ENABLED=false and the database failing:
- /date/2031-05-09 still shows Requirement 3's message.
- The matched control /date/2023-05-09 shows the "Saved horoscopes can't be loaded right now" state.

STEPS 5 and 6, the user's unmatched rows with saved horoscopes: PASS.
The user ran the Human Prerequisite query and supplied 5 rows:
- 79375fb5-3f5b-40f2-97ec-5cea6c431506, 1900-01-01;
- c82ee901-6fb3-430d-804f-2151621d9d18, 1946-06-25;
- 9bd536d1-243f-49e7-8c59-af75b6d76067, 1969-07-21;
- 49c7a5c0-c47e-4b98-932d-7c99c61b68c3, 1969-07-23;
- d8407973-a099-4b33-8bb2-ce6101bb5cb7, 1977-03-31.
All 10 production pages (/date/<d> and /reading/<id>) returned 200 and show Requirement 3's message, with
all 5 years linked by that page's month and day.
No horoscope text appears on any of them, measured against a matched control, /date/1969-07-20:
- horoscope paragraph elements (class paragraph): 0 on every page, against 3 on the control;
- reveal details: 0, against 1;
- "Revealed on request": 0;
- no "horoscope" key in the RSC payload;
- /reading pages have no form at all.
Also on the local build against the stand-in database, sentinel horoscope strings on rows with unmatched,
null, pre-1700-only and empty events appeared 0 times in each page's HTML, including the RSC payload.
- /date pages show Requirement 3's message; null events gave the "events unavailable" message on
  /reading.
- The matched control row's sentinel did render, 2 times, which proves the stand-in works.

STEP 7, phone 390x844: PASS.
- /date/2031-05-09, /date/1969-07-21 and /reading/9bd536d1-...: scrollWidth 390, the message wraps
  cleanly, and year links are 52x45.
- No console or page errors.

STEP 8, a hand-built POST to the cast action: PASS, on the local build. Not sent to production, to avoid
any risk of writing a horoscope there.
Setup:
- The action id came from the write form on the local matched page.
- curl --form-string posted "$ACTION_ID_4028b08d..." plus date.
- The stand-in PostgREST logged every request. OpenAI was refused at the fetch layer, and every attempt
  was logged.
Unmatched:
- date=2031-05-09 (also tried posted to /date/2023-05-09), and date=2031-01-01 (pre-1700 only) and
  date=2031-01-02 (empty).
- Each returned 303 to /date/<date>?error=We have no recorded events for this exact date, so we can't
  write an accurate horoscope for it.
- The only backend call was rpc/get_reading_by_date: no POST /rest/v1/readings, no set_reading_horoscope
  and no OpenAI call.
Failed lookup:
- date=2031-03-03 with Wikipedia blocked returned 303 with ?error=The events for this date couldn't be
  loaded..., after get_reading_by_date and one Wikipedia attempt.
- There was no insert and no OpenAI call.
Positive control:
- date=2023-05-09 (matched) did run POST /rest/v1/readings and then tried OpenAI, ending "Horoscope
  generation failed, try again."
- So the hand-built POST is a real action call, and the refusals happen before the insert.
On production, the redirect target /date/2031-05-09?error=... shows Requirement 3's message once in the
visible text, with no separate error banner, and scrollWidth 390.

OBSERVATIONS for Master Controller, not defects:
1. On /reading/[id] there is no date picker; the page has no form at all. Yet Requirements 3 and 4 say
   "Pick a different date above". Requirement 10 mandates that wording, so this is a copy decision.
   Screenshot: s39-_reading_9bd536d1_243f_49e7_8c59_af75b6d76067-1280.png.
2. QA1's Q1 is still open: an older matched horoscope behind a newer unmatched one is unreachable.
   - I did not test it live, because no supplied date has that mix.
   - None of the 5 supplied dates matched on a fresh lookup either, so none offered a duplicate write.
